### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **24** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**35** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6d7f4df3c91c0d4e7d0a40c3b5dc796290e90a2d`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6d7f4df3c91c0d4e7d0a40c3b5dc796290e90a2d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f98acedc60dee12a94e9b5193396536a9a58c7dc` — the merge of head `9107ffa4c9afb74bd62fb8183df28110ab4cf74b` into base `6d7f4df3c91c0d4e7d0a40c3b5dc796290e90a2d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f98acedc60dee12a94e9b5193396536a9a58c7dc && git checkout f98acedc60dee12a94e9b5193396536a9a58c7dc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6d7f4df3c91c0d4e7d0a40c3b5dc796290e90a2d 9107ffa4c9afb74bd62fb8183df28110ab4cf74b && git checkout -B drift-repro 6d7f4df3c91c0d4e7d0a40c3b5dc796290e90a2d && git merge --no-ff 9107ffa4c9afb74bd62fb8183df28110ab4cf74b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6d7f4df3c91c0d4e7d0a40c3b5dc796290e90a2d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6d7f4df3c91c0d4e7d0a40c3b5dc796290e90a2d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9107ffa4c9afb74bd62fb8183df28110ab4cf74b`
Local-runs: none

Rendered 2026-10-13T13:31Z by the adopting seat's session, read-only, adversarially: card #23214's body and every comment (triage `6143014548`, claim `6143999704`, the round-1 stop `6144314970`, ruling `6144365165`, the slice-1 claim `6144390225`, the dev's report `6146257839`, and the ACCEPT `6146305565` read as a claim to test); PR #23211's record `6142424713` as the pattern and precedent; PR #23263's body, file list and the net diff of `refs/pull/23263/head` against its merge base `afbf960c26` (12 files, +725 / -25, read whole); the head's files where the diff lacked context (`domains/meta.ts`, `data.ts`, `ui.ts`, `i18n.ts`, `security.ts`, `packages.ts`, `http-dispatcher.ts`, `error-envelope.ts`, `action-execution.ts`, `rest-server.ts` at every `refuseRepeatedQueryParams` site, `meta-item-read-gate.ts`, `query-multiplicity.ts`, `index.ts`, `package.json`, `package-routes.ts`, the Hono adapter's catch-all, the three changeset gates' sources, `spec`'s status-to-code map); card #23265; and the head's check-runs, polled four times over twenty-five minutes until every run had concluded. Nothing was built, run, re-run or ablated. The dev's BASE/HEAD differential and six ablations were not re-run and are not needed: each claim they support is re-derived from the diff below.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, named right or wrong against the handlers' ACTUAL read points on both transports.

1. **Per route, the multiplicity set equals the twin's declared set — right, on every route with a twin.** Each dispatcher set, read off the head's code, beside its `RestServer` twin's list at the head:
   - `GET /meta/object/:name/state/:field`: `['from']` on both (the dispatcher reads only `query.from`, `meta.ts:1026`; REST `:8232`).
   - `GET /meta/_drafts`: `['packageId', 'type']` on both (the dispatcher reads only those two, `:1920`-`:1921`; REST `:5863`).
   - `GET /meta/:type`: `['package', 'preview', 'object', 'include', 'id']` on both (REST `:6017`). The dispatcher's reads after the decision: `package` through `metaItemPackageBinding` (`:2005`), `preview` as a string (`:2051`), and `id`, `object`, `include` inside the shared `createMetaListAnswer` (`meta-item-read-gate.ts:3321`, `:3333`, `:3356`), which receives the same `query` object the decision unwrapped in place, so a one-element array reaches the chain as the string. `locale` is read by `metaRequestLocale` and is deliberately outside the `once` list on both transports (typeof-guarded to the default; pinned). No name read is outside the set; no name in the set goes unread.
   - `GET /meta/book/:name/tree`: `['package']` on both (`:1061`; REST `:6293`).
   - `GET /security/suggested-bindings`: `['status', 'packageId']` on both, in that order (`security.ts:163`; REST `:11612`).
   - `GET /packages`: `['status', 'type']` beside the existing `enabled` refusal. REST has no second reading of this door: `package-routes.ts` records that the dispatcher domain is the single implementation its registrar shadows, so the twin is the domain's own `enabled` refusal, mirrored line for line, including the bare `deps.error(message, 400)` whose code derives as `VALIDATION_ERROR` from `spec`'s `HttpStatusErrorCodeMap[400]` (pinned).
   - `GET /data/:object`, the filter slot: `FILTER_SLOT_QUERY_PARAMS` is `['where', 'filter', 'filters', '$filter']` (the `where` slot's one alias is `filter`, `data-engine.zod.ts:603`); the pins cover all four. `select` and `expand` are not in that list, are never touched, and are pinned as arrays. The #6878 ruling's multi-valued names are untouched; `/data/:object/:id`'s `select` and `expand` pass-through is not in the diff.
   - The four by-name `/meta` doors are not in the diff and keep `metaItemQueryRefusal`.
   No name is refused that a twin accepts repeated, and no legitimately multi-valued name is touched.
2. **The three dispatcher-only reads — right under route rule 5 and the #6878 ruling.** `/ui/view/:object` `?type` (REST mounts `/ui/view/:object/:type` only, `rest-server.ts:8648`; no REST route reads `?type`) and the two `/i18n` query-locale arms (REST mounts no `/i18n` route) have no twin. Each handler reads the name as ONE value, and after slice 2 it will SEE the repeat as an array: the #6878 ruling's condition for refusing is met at the read point itself, and the alternative (last-wins or first-wins) is the silent choice between two expressed intents the #7390 ruling refused. `?type` is read only when the path names no type (`ui.ts:106`): a repeated `?type` beside a path type is never read, and is pinned as ignored. `?locale` is read only when the path names no locale (`i18n.ts:140`, `:168`); a repeat used to throw inside `resolveLocale` and surface as the catch-all's 500, which is a defect by any reading, so a located 400 is strictly better. An empty array reads as absent on all three, as `readSingleQueryValue` reads it. Right.
3. **Ordering against the calls each refusal feeds — right on all ten routes.** Each refusal answers before the protocol or service read it protects, and each refusal pin asserts the service was never called: state before `getObjectQL` and `legalNextStates`; `_drafts` before `listDrafts`; the list before `refuseUnknownMetaListType` and `getMetaItems`; the book tree before `getMetaItems`; `/ui` before `getUiView`; `/i18n` before `getTranslations` and `getFieldLabels`; `/security` before the status vocabulary and `listAudienceBindingSuggestions`; `/packages` before `getAllPackages`; `/data` before `callData`.
4. **Ordering against the gates the twins answer after — right, with the `/data` case judged separately in item 5.** On `/meta` all four decisions sit after the anonymous deny (`meta.ts:939`-`:946`) and the type-level read refusal (`:960`), which precede every branch; `_drafts` additionally after its capability 403, the protocol resolve and the `listDrafts` probe, exactly where REST asks it (`:5844`-`:5863`); the book tree after `resolveProtocol`, as REST (`:6291`-`:6293`); the list as the branch's first statement, which is REST's handler's first statement after the auth middleware (`:5994`), so on both transports arity precedes the unknown-type refusal. `/security` sits after the anonymous deny and the service probe, before the status vocabulary, the same order as REST (`:11606`-`:11612`). `/packages` sits after `requireReadCapability`, where the `enabled` refusal already sits, for the reason that site records. `/i18n` sits after the anonymous deny and the service availability gate. `/ui` has no gate of its own before the branch; the refusal precedes the 501 for a host without `getUiView`, the same class as PR #23211's `/layers` placement: a malformed request to a host with no handler answers 400 where it answered 501. The one caller who reaches a `/meta` decision unauthenticated is the public-audience exemption on a `book` or `doc` list and on the book tree (`isPublicAudienceRead`), which REST's `enforceAuth` exempts by the same predicate, so the arity refusal precedes the audience gate on both transports alike. Every refusal body is the name and its count: it discloses nothing about existence, exposure or capability, so no caller learns from a 400 anything a prior gate withholds.
5. **The `/data` filter slot's placement — judged explicitly: a changed order for a malformed request only; not a defect.** REST's list handler answers `enforceAuth` (401), then `enforceApiAccess` (the ADR-0049 exposure 403), then `assertFilterParamSuppliedOnce` (`rest-server.ts:8726`-`:8761`). The dispatcher's `/data` domain has no anonymous deny of its own (`dispatch()` defers to upstream auth, `http-dispatcher.ts:1519`; the exposure gate is inside `callData`, `action-execution.ts:293`-`:304`), so the new refusal precedes BOTH the exposure 403 and whatever an anonymous caller is answered inside `callData`. The dev declared the 403 half; this record names the 401 half too. What a caller can learn: nothing. The 400 is answered regardless of exposure, so it carries no exposure fact; the 403 a well-formed request still receives is the only carrier of that fact, and it is unchanged. REST itself is not uniform here: its own `DELETE /data/:object/:id` asks `refuseRepeatedQueryParams(['expectedVersion'])` BEFORE `enforceApiAccess` (`:9061`, `:9067`). Accepted as recorded in the acceptance notes.
6. **One source — right; the re-point is proven by the diff itself.** `META_QUERY_ARITY_DOORS` and `metaQueryArityRefusal` live beside `metaItemQueryRefusal`, and rule 2 of that decision is now the same private `repeatedOnceRefusal` the new decision calls: the moved loop is the old loop verbatim (same `Array.isArray` check, same `readSingleQueryValue`, same `repeatedQueryParamMessage(name, read.count)`, same in-place `record[name] = read.value`, same `rule: 'repeated-parameter'`). `rest-server.ts` changes four lines, each `refuseRepeatedQueryParams(req, res, LITERAL)` to `refuseRepeatedQueryParams(req, res, metaReadGate.META_QUERY_ARITY_DOORS.DOOR)`, and each constant's array is the literal it replaces, element for element and in the same order (`drafts`, `list`, `book-tree`, `state`). Since `refuseRepeatedQueryParams` iterates the names in order over an identical array, the answers are byte-identical by construction; the dev's 50-case differential is consistent and was not needed. No other spelling of any of the four lists exists at the head outside the gate module and its pins (repo grep). The `['preview']` list at `:10100` is the analytics dataset route, not a `/meta` list. The one list now spelled on both transports is `/security`'s `['status', 'packageId']` (`security.ts:163`, `rest-server.ts:11612`), judged in ③.
7. **The `/data` filter slot imports the rule — right, and the unwrap changes no other read.** `data.ts:21` imports `assertFilterParamSuppliedOnce` from `@objectstack/rest` (the runtime already depends on it, `workspace:*`); `FILTER_SLOT_QUERY_PARAMS` is not re-spelled anywhere in the runtime. The rule runs on `listQuery = { ...query }`, a shallow copy, and `callData` receives that copy: before this diff the handler spread `{ ...query }` inline at the same call, so the copy semantics are unchanged and the dispatcher's own `query` object is never written. The list branch reads nothing else from `query` and returns. The only new behaviour beside the refusal is the one-element unwrap on the copy, which is REST's behaviour since #7390 and is declared in the changeset and pinned. The throw is answered as `deps.error(e.message, 400, { code: e.code })`, so the code is `INVALID_FILTER` and the sentence is REST's `repeatedFilterParamMessage`; the pin computes the expected pair by calling the same imported rule, never by re-spelling it.
8. **The published surface — right as graded.** `packages/rest/package.json` publishes the single `.` entry (`dist/index.*`, not private, unchanged by this diff). `src/index.ts` gains exactly three value names: `assertFilterParamSuppliedOnce` (a module export of `query-multiplicity.ts` since #7390; that file is untouched), `META_QUERY_ARITY_DOORS` and `metaQueryArityRefusal` (new in the gate module). The index diff is +14 / -1, the one removed line being the re-spelled export that keeps `refuseRepeatedQueryParams` and `repeatedQueryParamMessage`; nothing leaves the entry, and no type joins it. The dev's CJS supplement (both `dist/index.cjs` load, rest's carrying the three names) is consistent with the head's `Build Core` and type-check runs. Two consistency notes, neither a finding: the type `MetaQueryArityDoor` is a module export left off the entry's `export type` block, exactly as `MetaItemQueryDoor` is (PR #23211's record, item 8), so a consumer derives it from the function's parameter type; and the entry's new comment at `index.ts:140`-`:141` says "the two `/meta` doors that are not by-name (the list and the book tree)" where the constant declares four doors. Comment only; the constant, its docblock and the pins agree on four.
9. **The pins — right, both halves per route.** `dispatcher-query-arity.test.ts` boots the real `HttpDispatcher` as `createHonoApp` does, with recording doubles and an authoring caller, and pins per route the status, `success: false`, the nested `error.code`, the exact sentence and the service never called, beside a preservation pin on the arguments the service received for one value (and for a one-element array where that read changed). `/packages` runs over a real `SchemaRegistry`. The set itself is pinned once (`META_QUERY_ARITY_DOORS` equals the four lists) and read from the constant for the per-name cases, so a name added to the list is pinned without a second spelling. `meta-query-arity-doors.test.ts` pins the decision as data and drives `RestServer`'s four handlers to show each refuses exactly the shared names with the nested 400 before any protocol read, plus one-value preservation. Consistent with route rule 5's two halves.
10. **The caller census — holds on what this tree can show.** The names the SDK writes are single-set spellings; no in-repo literal repeats one of these names on these routes; and on a shipped host only `GET /packages` through `plugin-hono-server`'s mounts (`dispatcher-plugin.ts:1392`-`:1398`) receives arrays today, where a repeated `status` or `type` answered an empty 200 and now answers the located 400. Every other point is behind `createHonoApp`'s catch-all, which still flattens (`packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts:789`), so the narrowing is visible there only after slice 2. The changeset says so.

### ② Semver level

**Right.** Judged against AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, the two changeset gates' sources, and PR #23211's record.

- `'@objectstack/rest': minor` — three new value exports widen the published entry; `Clause-②: yes` takes at least `minor`. Right.
- `'@objectstack/runtime': minor` — ten dispatcher routes' accept sets narrow (seventeen names, the filter slot counted once), which is BREAKING, shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` records at its header (`:58`-`:66`); the same grade PR #23211 landed with. Right.
- `fix(runtime)!:` — the PR title and the changeset's first line carry the bang. Right.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on PR line 2 and once in the changeset — `clause2-line.mjs` names this spelling as a diff that widens one surface and narrows another, which is exactly this one. Right.
- One ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, in the comment form the gate reads, with its facts: `packages/spec` is untouched (file list), no export is removed (the index diff removes nothing), both packages publish, no ADR-0087 id is named. The body's remedy ("send each name once") is an imperative request sentence with no FROM-to-TO rewrite pair, the shape PR #23211's record judged honest for the same category; `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are `success` on this head. The launch-window `**BREAKING**` line is present once. No `skip-changeset` label. Right.
- Pre mode changes nothing about the grade: `.changeset/pre.json` reads `mode: pre`, tag `next`, on this head, both packages sit at `18.0.0-next.0`, and the level still decides the CHANGELOG section and the breaking classification consumers read, as PR #23211's record reasoned. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

The report `6146257839` has no `open_questions`, which is right: ruling `6144365165` answered both questions round 1 raised, and this head is slice 1 of that answer. Every dev deviation and finding, answered or escalated:

- **The `_drafts` and state lists moved beyond the two the dispatch named** — right. The ruling's general rule ("where `RestServer` spells an arity list in `rest-server.ts`, that list moves beside the shared decision") covers every `/meta` door whose twin spells one; the claim's `rest-server.ts` surface is "the arity lists' spelling"; and the move is spelling-only (item 6). Leaving two of four `/meta` lists inline would have been the half-measure the ruling's one-source rule exists to end. No action.
- **`/security`'s two-name list kept at the dispatcher's read point** — acceptable at this head, and the one residual this record carries. The ruling placed S1 and S2 in the no-shared-list group and named `meta-item-read-gate.ts`, a `/meta` module, as the home; a security route does not belong there, and inventing a new home was outside the claim. The result is one two-name list spelled on both transports, which is the shape the one-source rule is against, declared in the acceptance notes. Carried for the seat: a shared home for non-`/meta` arity lists, or a re-point of REST `:11612` to a constant the dispatcher imports, in a later slice. Not a finding against this head.
- **Three exports, not one** — right. The ruling itself prescribes that "both transports import" the moved lists, which needs the list and the decision on the entry; the claim's "one new export" counted the filter rule alone. Three is the honest count, the PR, the changeset and the marker all declare three, and the grade is unchanged. No action.
- **Two scratch files outside the surface, deleted** — verified: the PR's file list is the twelve paths the report names, with no scratch file among them, and the three-dot diff adds no other path. No action.
- **The `/data` ordering** — judged in ① item 5, including the 401 half the dev did not name. No action.
- **One merge of `main`** — verified: `9107ffa4c9`'s second parent `afbf960c26` is the merge base itself, so the three-dot diff is the five branch commits and nothing else; the merge commit carries no trailers, as a git-generated merge does, and the five authored commits carry `Claude-Session` and the model-free `Co-authored-by`. No action.
- **`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED** — declared with its prerequisite reason and a scoped supplement (both CJS entries load; rest's carries the three names), and answered by the head's build and lint families: `Build Core`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, every `Type Check` run and `Check Changeset` are `success`. This record did not map the gate to one named run. No action.
- **The class-a out-of-scope finding: the dispatcher's `DELETE /data/:object/:id` drops `expectedVersion` and `If-Match`** — verified at the head: `data.ts:130` calls `callData('delete', { object, id })`, `action-execution.ts:399` forwards `{ object, id, environmentId, context }` with no version, and REST's twin reads `?expectedVersion` or `If-Match` behind its arity gate and forwards it (`rest-server.ts:9061`-`:9072`). The dev measured it at `createHonoApp`, a public door, so under Prime Directive #10 it is a card, not a note, and the ruling's "report it if measurable" is met. The card exists: #23265 (`finding`, filed 2026-10-13T13:12Z by the seat), carrying the repro, the governing text, the acceptance and a dedupe line; triage grades it. Right, and rightly not fixed here: the dispatch made it read-only. No action on this head.
- **The docs-drift check** — a flag, not a verdict (`Flag docs affected by code changes` is `success`); its 35 pages were not walked. Nothing in this diff changes a documented input: a repeated single-valued query name was never a documented accept, so no hand-written page can have stated the behaviour this PR removes. No action.
- **Check-runs on `9107ffa4c9`** — latest run per name, polled last at 2026-10-13T13:31Z, every run concluded: 31 `success` (`Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, every Lint and Type Check run, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Test Core` 1/6 through 6/6, the last shard completing at 2026-10-13T13:29:54Z, the single-writer, card-claim and part-of guards), 8 `skipped` (`Console Pin Gate`, the live-database and opt-in gates, as this diff's paths warrant), none failed, none in progress. Three earlier polls over twenty-five minutes saw `Test Core (3/6)` still running; the gate verdicts are the check-runs', and they are green. No action.
- **Scope and shape** — 12 files, all inside the claim's surface; 750 changed lines, under the 3,000 threshold; no governed path (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` is `success`); `Part of #23214` on line 1 is right because slice 2 ends the card, and `Part-of PR must not also close its card` is `success`; the PR is a draft with no review submitted; `needs:contract-review` was the seat's write in the ACCEPT.
- **Residuals this record adds for the seat**, neither a finding against this head: the `/security` list's second spelling (above), the `MetaQueryArityDoor` type off the entry beside its `MetaItemQueryDoor` sibling, and the "two doors" comment at `index.ts:140` that should say four.

Everything in ① and ③ holds, and ② holds. Nothing in this record is a finding the seat must act on before landing; the residuals are follow-ups.
